findings.evidence: `Kernel/Basic.lean:7-9` imports only `Mathlib.Analysis.RCLike.Basic`, `Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Order`, `Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.PosDef`; the file's own module docstring now says "A kernel is represented directly as a matrix, so the API uses Mathlib's `Matrix.PosSemidef` rather than introducing a second predicate." `TauCeti/Analysis/Matrix/` already exists (`UnitaryGroup.lean`).
findings.fix: Move the index-type-generic `Matrix.PosSemidef` lemmas to a matrix home — e.g. a new `TauCeti/Analysis/Matrix/PosSemidef.lean` alongside the existing `TauCeti/Analysis/Matrix/UnitaryGroup.lean` (the RCLike/`Analysis.Matrix.Order` dependency rules out `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean`) — and leave in `PositiveDefinite/Kernel/` only what is genuinely kernel-specific (`Finsupp.lean`, `Radical.lean`, `Kolmogorov.lean`, and the subtraction-kernel section of `Bounds.lean`).
findings.issue: After the wrapper is deleted, this file's declarations (`posSemidef_conj_mul`:96, `posSemidef_one`:104, `posSemidef_const_of_nonneg`:114, `posSemidef_iff`:124) are general facts about Mathlib's `Matrix.PosSemidef` over an arbitrary index type — no kernel notion remains in the file, and it imports nothing from `TauCeti/` (lines 7–9 are all Mathlib). Same for `Kernel/Closure.lean` (`posSemidef_prod`:52, `posSemidef_sum_smul`, `posSemidef_pow`, `posSemidef_sum_conj_mul`, `posSemidef_prod_conj_mul`:104, `posSemidef_sum_smul_conj_mul`), the first section of `Kernel/Bounds.lean` (`posSemidef_normSq_le`:66, `posSemidef_eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_left`:91/`_right`:101, `posSemidef_norm_le_one_of_apply_self_eq_one`), and `Limits.lean` `posSemidef_of_tendsto`:58. Broadly useful matrix API depending on no analysis theory is hidden in a positive-definite-function/kernel subdirectory where a reader looking for PSD-matrix lemmas will not find it and will re-prove them.

findings.evidence: grep for `posSemidef_iff|posSemidef_conj_mul|posSemidef_one|posSemidef_const_of_nonneg` over `TauCeti/` returns no hit in any of these five files; `CharFun/PositiveDefinite.lean:8` is `public import TauCeti.Analysis.PositiveDefinite.Basic`, whose line 10 is `public import ...Kernel.Basic`, and `Limits.lean:7` is `public import ...Function.Kernel` with the same transitive path.
findings.fix: Drop the import in `Limits.lean:8` and `CharFun/PositiveDefinite.lean:9` (both already get `Matrix.PosSemidef` transitively — via `Function.Kernel`→`PositiveDefinite.Basic` and via `CharFun.PosDef`/`PositiveDefinite.Basic` respectively). In `Gaussian/Regularization.lean:9`, `Kolmogorov.lean:7` and `Kernel/Bounds.lean:7` replace it with `public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.PosDef`, which is the only thing still being consumed through it.
findings.issue: The PR deleted this module's only uses of `Kernel.Basic` (`isPositiveDefiniteKernel_def`, `isPositiveDefiniteKernel_conj_symm`) but kept `public import TauCeti.Analysis.PositiveDefinite.Kernel.Basic`. The same holds in four other modules: `Bochner/CharFun/PositiveDefinite.lean:9`, `Bochner/Gaussian/Regularization.lean:9`, `Kernel/Kolmogorov.lean:7`, and `Kernel/Bounds.lean:7` — none now references any declaration of `Kernel.Basic` (`posSemidef_conj_mul` / `posSemidef_one` / `posSemidef_const_of_nonneg` / `posSemidef_iff`).

findings.evidence: `Gaussian/Basic.lean:123` uses `charFun_posSemidef`; `grep -n "theorem charFun_posSemidef"` → `TauCeti/Analysis/Bochner/CharFun/PosDef.lean:124`. `CharFun/PositiveDefinite.lean` declares only `charFun_star_kernel_posSemidef_of_star_eq_neg`, `charFun_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg`, `continuous_charFun_and_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg`, none of which appears in `Gaussian/Basic.lean`.
findings.issue: `public import TauCeti.Analysis.Bochner.CharFun.PositiveDefinite` is now over-broad: the PR replaced the file's only use of that module (`charFun_isPositiveDefiniteKernel`) with `charFun_posSemidef`, which lives in `CharFun/PosDef.lean:124`. None of the three declarations of `CharFun/PositiveDefinite.lean` is used here.

summary: Removing the kernel wrapper turned four modules' contents into generic Matrix.PosSemidef lemmas that no longer belong under Analysis/PositiveDefinite/Kernel/, and left six imports that the migration made dead or over-broad.
